manifest.title: High-Efficiency Methylammonium Lead Iodide Perovskite Solar Cells with a Compact TiO2 Electron Transport Layer (SYNTHETIC)

paragraphs.text: We report perovskite solar cells based on methylammonium lead iodide that achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.1% under standard 1-sun illumination at initial measurement.
Organic-inorganic lead halide perovskites have attracted intense research interest owing to their high absorption coefficient and long carrier diffusion lengths.
A compact TiO2 electron transport layer was deposited on fluorine-doped tin oxide glass by spray pyrolysis, and the methylammonium lead iodide absorber was coated on top of this layer.
The precursor solution contained methylammonium iodide and lead iodide in a 1:1 molar ratio dissolved in dimethylformamide.
Champion devices showed a stabilized power output of 20.4% measured during 60 s of continuous 1-sun illumination.
The current-voltage scan showed negligible hysteresis, and the hysteresis index was not reported in this study.
External quantum efficiency exceeded 90% across the visible range for the champion device.
X-ray diffraction confirmed the tetragonal phase of the perovskite film after annealing at 100 °C for 10 min.
Unencapsulated devices retained 85% of their initial efficiency after 200 h of storage in dry nitrogen.
These results establish methylammonium lead iodide devices with compact TiO2 layers as a viable route to high-efficiency photovoltaics.

manifest.title: Damp-Heat Stability of MAPbI3 Solar Cells on Mesoporous TiO2 Scaffolds (SYNTHETIC)

paragraphs.text: We assess the damp-heat stability of MAPbI3 solar cells fabricated on mesoporous TiO2 scaffolds, finding that the champion device retained 18.7% of its initial power conversion efficiency after 500 h at 85 °C and 85% relative humidity.
Perovskite modules deployed outdoors experience sustained heat and moisture stress that accelerates degradation.
A mesoporous TiO2 scaffold with a particle size of 20 nm was screen-printed over a compact blocking layer on fluorine-doped tin oxide glass.
The MAPbI3 film was formed by spin coating a lead-rich precursor followed by vapor annealing in methylammonium iodide.
Initial power conversion efficiency under 1-sun illumination averaged 19.6% across eight devices.
After 500 h of damp-heat testing, the champion device retained 18.7% of its initial power conversion efficiency.
Scanning electron microscopy showed full infiltration of MAPbI3 into the mesoporous scaffold.
Degradation was dominated by moisture ingress at the scaffold edges rather than intrinsic decomposition of the absorber.
X-ray diffraction of aged films showed no detectable lead iodide peak after 500 h of damp-heat exposure.
Encapsulation strategies will be required before these devices can be considered for outdoor deployment.
